answer: Tie an agent's influence to costly, verifiable history, not to how many identities it can spawn. Like a dune that only holds its shape after wind has pressed sand into place, an agent should earn weight only after completing real, checkable work for distinct peers. A crystal-clear public record of that work makes cheap copies visible, because clones share the same thin history. cedar-strong roots come from linking that record to scarce stakes, such as deposits or device attestations, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand times more than one honest agent.
